en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Śrī Nārada said: O Brahmā, among the hosts of immortals headed by Indra, there is something most supreme and wonderful.
O Lord, please tell me that which is called the "Inexhaustible Armor."
"By wearing which and hearing which, a hero shall become the conqueror of the three worlds.
Brahmā said:
"Listen, O son, O best of sages, to this most wonderful armor (kavaca)."
And this Prajāpati [heard] from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa the armor of this Trailokyavijaya from the hosts of gods beginning with Indra. (3)
The seer (ṛṣi), the meter (chandas), and the deity (devatā) are eternally the Lord Nārāyaṇa.
Of this imperishable armor (kavaca) for the victory over the three worlds, Prajāpati is the seer;
Anuṣṭubh is the meter; and the Supreme Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is the deity.
The application is for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa during the recitation:
May Govinda protect my feet; may the Lord of the World protect my shanks. (4)
May Keśava protect my two thighs, and may Dāmodara protect my waist thereafter;
may Śrī Hari protect my face, and may Acyuta protect the region of my vital channels.
Likewise, Viṣṇu is on the left side and Sudarśana on the right;
Vāsudeva is at the base of the arms and Janārdana is in the heart.
May Varāha protect my throat, and Kṛṣṇa protect the circle of my face;
may Mādhava protect my ears, and Hṛṣīkeśa protect my nostrils.
May Nārāyaṇa protect my eyes; may he whose banner is Garuḍa protect my forehead;
may Keśava protect my cheeks, and likewise may Cakrapāṇi protect my head.
May Mādhava protect at dawn, Madhusūdana at midday,
Daityanāśa at the end of the day, and may Candramas protect at night.
Puṇḍarīkākṣa is in the east and Janārdana is in the northwest;
thus, my child, I have described to you the embodiment of the entire multitude of mantras.
Out of affection for you, I have told this; however, it must not be spoken of to anyone.
The practitioner who wears this armor upon his right arm—
The gods, humans, and Gandharvas are his sacrifices; of this there is no doubt.
A woman is on his left arm, and a man is on his right arm.
One should keep this meritorious armor secret; one shall become endowed with all perfections.
Whoever wears this armor, which is my own form, around the neck—
The practitioner attains victory in battle, in gambling, and in debate;
he certainly attains victory in every way, birth after birth. (14)
A sonless man obtains a son, and likewise his diseases shall be destroyed;
liberated from all afflictions, he goes to the world of Viṣṇu. || 15 ||
Thus ends the Śrīgopālākṣayakavaca as declared in the Brahmasaṃhitā.
